parameters.note: Rest between work sets, low volume and high intensity (coaching experience, K-49: 2-3 minutes; the aim is mechanical tension, not metabolic stress). The session's rest timer counts up and shows the band (K-405); the timer in the background and the Live Activity are K-411.

The quick RIR picker (B 6.5: one tap per set): 0, 1, 2 and 3+. The last choice means 3 or more and is logged as 3; work sets aim at 0-1 (target_rir_max, G1 K-5), so anything past 3 says the same thing: further from failure than planned.
NewSet.loadKg maximum: a heavier set would be refused by the server and lost from the queue.
NewSet.reps maximum. A set logged here has at least one rep: zero is not a set done.

The same as training.yaml (the engine's, K-218): the session summary (K-406) shows the estimated max of a set the way the engine reads it. Epley: load x (1 + reps to failure / 30), reps to failure = reps + RIR. MobileParameterMirrorTests keeps the two equal.
The same as training.yaml: no estimate past 10 reps to failure (Mayhew 2008).

The same as training.yaml: work sets end at RIR 0-1. The summary judges the effort against the planned RIR, and against this when the plan has none (a day gone from the program). MobileParameterMirrorTests keeps it equal.
The day's first move: 3-4 warm-ups (K-17); the low end, so the warm-up never tires.
Every other move: at least one warm-up (K-17).

Without a gym on the phone (K-421), warm-up loads round to this step: a pair of the smallest common kg plates. The gym's own weights come first (ADR-032).
The same in lb: a pair of 2.5 lb plates.
How far back a move's history and records reach (ADR-033 §1): a year of training; the server answers at most 400 days (keel.api.max-range-days).
A note on a set or a session (K-422): the contract's maxLength, the server's keel.training.max-note.
How many moves the session's 'Add a move' search shows (K-416): a short list to pick from with one tap (I2 A4: alternatives ready, no long search).
The name of the user's own move (K-416, ADR-035): the contract's maxLength, the server's keel.training.custom-exercise.max-name.
A move working these is a back move (K-418 tips): full range everywhere (K-50) except the back, where partial reps at the end of a set are fine (K-56).
One setup note (seat, pad, grip) kept on the phone (K-418, ADR-017): the same machine set the same way (K-38) needs a short mark like 'seat 4, pin 3'.

Each catalog muscle (data/muscles.yaml) as the areas of the muscle map's drawing (react-native-body-highlighter 3.2.0 slugs, K-418): the drawing has one area for all three delts and none for the lats alone.

A session open longer than this is not written to Apple Health (K-412): sets carry no times, so the finish is the only end the app knows, and a session left unfinished for days would be kept there as a days-long workout (U1). Derived: the program's sessions are around an hour (G1); four hours is well past any of them.

The same as windows.yaml (the engine's): progress is judged over 3 months, not week to week (coaching experience, K-25; 03 §2.7). The strength chart (K-604) spans this window. MobileParameterMirrorTests keeps the two equal.

The decision window the strength chart marks apart from the evaluation window (03 §5.2: decisions 1-2 weeks, evaluation 3 months, shown apart so weekly noise is not read as progress). Two, the longer end: the engine's training signals read about as far (plateau_sessions, 3 sessions at 2 a week; overtraining_missed_plan_weeks, 2). Display only; no call reads it.
